knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly contrasts named continuous distribution families on an interval support?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Support and generative story guide family choice. Normal-by-default or interchangeable families ignore positive support and hazard shape.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Match support/shape story; exponential for memoryless waiting times.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Normal-by-default or treating distinct continuous families as interchangeable.

choices.label: Named continuous families (Normal, lognormal, exponential, gamma, chi-square, t, F, beta, uniform continuous) share continuous support but differ in shape and scale stories: for example exponential models positive memoryless waiting times under constant hazard.
Normal is the default family for any positive quantity because symmetric all-real support is always adequate after standardisation.
Exponential and Normal are interchangeable for waiting times because both have a single numeric parameter.
Continuous families apply only to variables already transformed to z-scores; raw positive data must first be declared Normal.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Inter-claim waiting times are strictly positive and, under a constant hazard story, memoryless. Which statement is correct?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Memoryless positive waiting aligns with exponential. Normal CLT misuse, beta on unbounded times, or false lognormal exclusion are wrong.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Exponential for memoryless waiting; refuse Normal-by-default.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Normal-by-default or misplacing beta/lognormal for the stated story.

choices.label: Exponential fits first: positive support and memoryless waiting times under constant hazard. Refuse Normal-by-default because a symmetric all-real support model mismatches strictly positive waiting times.
Normal(μ, σ²) is appropriate because the central limit theorem always makes waiting times Normal regardless of support.
Beta distribution is required because waiting times are bounded between zero and one.
Lognormal is ruled out for any waiting-time problem because memoryless property implies exponential only when data are discrete.

worked_example.title: Select Exponential for memoryless waiting times
worked_example.problem_statement: Inter-claim waiting times are strictly positive and, under a constant hazard story, memoryless. Choose the matching continuous family. As a light numeric check, if the mean waiting time is 6 months, compute P(T > 6).

given.value: strictly positive waiting times; constant hazard; memoryless

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Match support and memorylessness to a named continuous family before evaluating the survival probability.

steps.label: Match story to family
steps.attempt_cue: Name the continuous family for positive memoryless waiting times.
steps.explanation: Exponential models positive memoryless waiting times under constant hazard. Normal has symmetric all-real support and is a poor default for strictly positive waits.

steps.label: Light numeric illustration P(T > 6)
steps.attempt_cue: For Exponential mean 6, evaluate the survival at t = 6.
steps.explanation: With mean θ = 6, P(T > t) = e^{−t/θ}. At the mean, survival equals e^{−1}. The numeric check illustrates the chosen family; family selection remains the LO hinge.

steps.label: Refuse Normal-by-default
steps.attempt_cue: State the support mismatch for a Normal waiting-time model.
steps.explanation: A Normal model allows negative waiting times and is not memoryless. That mismatches the stated positive constant-hazard story.
steps.calculation: Normal support includes negatives; not memoryless → refuse

worked_example.final_answer: Choose Exponential for positive memoryless waiting times; with mean 6 months, P(T > 6) ≈ 0.3679. Refuse Normal-by-default for this story.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Defaulting to a Normal waiting-time model because it is familiar, ignoring that waiting times are strictly positive and memoryless under constant hazard.
